request.title: Why Cats Can't Taste Sweetness
request.narration: Your cat can't taste sugar. Here's why. Cats are obligate carnivores. Meat is their main fare. Their sweet-taste equipment is missing a critical part. In 2005, researchers examined the gene for Tas1r2, one of two proteins that build a working sweet receptor. In cats, that gene has a 247-base-pair deletion and premature stop signals. It is a pseudogene, not expressed. The partner gene, Tas1r3, is still expressed. But without both halves, the receptor cannot detect sugars. Sweetness has no channel to the brain. The same broken gene appeared in six domestic cats, a tiger, and a cheetah. It is not pickiness. It is deep cat biology. No sweet tooth; just a carnivore's toolkit.
